days.title: build your system
days.quote: The height of sophistication is simplicity.
days.quote_note: American writer, politician, diplomat and public intellectual. 1903–1987.
content: Anything complex is simplified by a system, broken into bite-sized pieces. That is how this challenge gets done.
Your system starts with one habit: small enough to keep on your hardest day, big enough to create daily momentum.
Open your tracker in the Progress tab: find the gaps, and close them.
Last week you made the promise. This week you build what sustains it.
days.affirmation: I keep it simple, and I keep it daily.

fields.prompt: Pick the habit that starts your system.
Your habit, in one line, small enough for your hardest day.
How sure are you that you’ll do it on your worst day?

days.action: Under 8? Make it smaller. Then do it today and tick it off here before you sleep.
pending_approval: Clare Boothe Luce as a new voice

days.title: design your space
days.quote: Environment is the invisible hand that shapes human behavior.
days.quote_note: American writer on habits and author of Atomic Habits. Born 1986.
content: Your space makes more of your choices than you do.
The phone by the bed, the shoes by the door, the bowl on the bench: each is a decision already made.
Leave the room as it is, and it keeps choosing for you. Design it so your new habits become the easy choice.
On Day 1 you pictured the space to THRIVE. Today you start building it, one object at a time.
days.affirmation: I design my space, and my space carries me.

fields.prompt: Which space shapes your habit most?
Which moves will you make?
options: Move a distraction out of sight
Set it out the night before

fields.prompt: The one change you’ll make, in one line.

days.action: Pics or it didn’t happen. Tonight, take a before of every space in your sanctuary, make your change, then take at least one after as evidence for tomorrow’s habit.

days.title: learn from every day
content: Ten days in, every day has left you something: the days you kept show you what works, and any that slipped show you exactly where to build.
A missed day becomes a lesson the moment you review it to find why you avoided it.
How you respond is yours to choose. Read your days, and the road gets clearer with every one.
days.affirmation: When I learn, I build. What I build, I keep.

fields.prompt: What helped on your best days?
What got in the way on the harder days?
Your lesson, in one line: next time I will…

days.action: Write your lesson where you’ll see it, and use it on tomorrow’s habit, whatever today held.

action_proof.text: In a study of new habits, missing one day made no real difference to how they formed.
action_proof.source: Lally et al., European Journal of Social Psychology, 2010

days.title: momentum over motivation
days.quote: If I only ran on the days I felt motivated to run, I wouldn’t run very much.
days.quote_note: Australian ultramarathon runner and 2026 Young Australian of the Year, who ran 3,952 km across Australia in 47 days. Born 1999.
content: Momentum over motivation: you build momentum, and momentum drives motivation.
Motivation arrives when it likes. Your system arrives every day: one habit, one cue, one tick.
Routine is built on the days you least feel like it, and rhythm grows from routine.
Keep the system running, and motivation catches up with you.
days.affirmation: I keep the system, and the system keeps me.

fields.prompt: How steady has your system been this week?
What will your habit follow each day?
Your cue, in one line: After I ___, I will ___.

days.action: Do your habit today straight after your cue, and tick it off the moment it’s done.

days.title: decide it in advance
days.quote: It is in your moments of decision that your destiny is shaped.
days.quote_attribution: Tony Robbins, Awaken the Giant Within (1991)
content: The hardest moment to decide is the moment you’re in it: tired, rushed, tempted.
So decide now, while you’re clear. When the obstacle comes, your answer is already waiting.
An excuse needs a gap to grow in. A plan made in advance leaves it no room.
On Day 5 you named your excuses. Today you give each one its answer, before it speaks.
days.affirmation: I decide before the moment decides for me.

fields.prompt: Which moment is most likely to stop you?
Your plan, in one line: If ___, then I will ___.
Where will your plan live?

days.action: Put your plan in place today, and read it aloud twice before bed tonight.

action_proof.text: Across 94 studies, people who made if-then plans reached their goals more often.
action_proof.source: Gollwitzer & Sheeran, Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 2006

days.title: one notch up
days.quote: Life is like riding a bicycle. To keep your balance you must keep moving.
days.quote_attribution: Albert Einstein, letter to his son Eduard (1930)
content: Twelve days of showing up have built something that carries you now: momentum.
Balance comes from moving. Every tick keeps you steady, and every kept promise makes the next one believable.
Today you add one notch to what you already do.
Tomorrow you look back at the road. Today you give it something worth looking at.
days.affirmation: I do better, I do more, I’m better than yesterday.

fields.prompt: Rate each of these today.
Your notch up today:
One thing from these two weeks the Day 1 you would be proud of.

days.action: Do your notched-up habit today, and tick it off before dinner.

days.title: reflection
framing: Fourteen days in, and your witness checks in today.
Tell them what you promised and what you did, plainly.
Every tool you picked up this week is still in your hands.

fields.prompt: What did I learn?
What did I love?
What can I do better?
